title: Gadag Raitha Samparka Kendra agricultural services
content: Gadag's Agriculture Department says Raitha Samparka Kendras are established at hobli level to provide updated crop-production information, arrange critical agricultural inputs, offer primary soil and seed testing, and connect farmers with public and private sector technologies. This describes the local extension model rather than district crop production totals.
source_org: Gadag District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district portal page is undated and does not report service coverage or current facility counts.
keywords: Gadag Raitha Samparka Kendra soil testing seed testing crop production inputs agriculture extension North Karnataka

title: Hiriyur agricultural research station crops and varieties
content: The University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences, Shivamogga lists ZAHRS Hiriyur as a research station established in 1916. Its crop portfolio includes groundnut, millets, Bengal gram, sunflower and castor, alongside fruits, vegetables, coconut and arecanut. The university page names groundnut varieties SahyadriDurga, Kadiri Lepakshi and DH-256; finger-millet variety KMR-340 White Ragi; Bengal-gram variety NBeG 47; red-gram BRG-5; and castor hybrid HCH-6.
source_org: University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences, Shivamogga
uncertainty: The page does not give release years or trial conditions for the named varieties; no yield or production claims are included.
keywords: Hiriyur Chitradurga ZAHRS groundnut millet ragi KMR-340 Bengal gram sunflower research varieties Uttara Karnataka

title: RSFH-1887 sunflower hybrid developed at Raichur
content: The University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur catalogue identifies RSFH-1887 as a sunflower hybrid developed at the Main Agricultural Research Station, Raichur, for Karnataka Zones 1 and 2. The catalogue reports a seed-yield potential of 25 quintals per hectare and moderate resistance to necrosis, sunflower leaf curl and Alternaria diseases. The yield figure is a variety-potential statement, not an observed district-wide yield.
source_title: Crop Varieties Released from UAS, Raichur (2009-10 to 2018-19)
source_org: University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur
reporting_year: Catalogue period 2009-10 to 2018-19; individual release year not stated
uncertainty: The catalogue entry is on page 6. It gives a potential, not district production, and does not state the individual release year or trial year.
keywords: Raichur RSFH-1887 sunflower hybrid yield potential 25 quintals hectare necrosis leaf curl Alternaria UAS Raichur

title: SCS 793 cotton cultivar developed at Raichur
content: The University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur catalogue says SCS 793 was developed under the All India Coordinated Research Project on Cotton at the Main Agricultural Research Station, Raichur, for Zones 2 and 3. It reports seed-cotton yield 22.6 percent above the Sahana local control and 24.1 percent above the Surabhi zonal control. These are catalogue comparisons, not district production statistics.
source_title: Crop Varieties Released from UAS, Raichur (2009-10 to 2018-19)
source_org: University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur
reporting_year: Catalogue period 2009-10 to 2018-19; individual release year not stated

title: Gokak Falls in Belagavi district
content: The Belagavi district tourism portal lists Gokak Falls among the district's natural attractions. It places the falls about 60 kilometres from Belagavi city and Gokak Road railway station about 10 kilometres away. The portal also names Jamboti Falls as another nearby natural attraction.
source_org: Belagavi District Administration, Government of Karnataka
reporting_year: Not stated by source; travel distances on an undated tourism page
uncertainty: The tourism page is undated and provides visitor-location information rather than hydrological measurements.

title: Almatti Dam and the Upper Krishna Irrigation Project
content: Vijayapura's district portal describes Almatti Dam on the Krishna River as the main reservoir of the Upper Krishna Irrigation Project and says the dam project was completed in July 2005. It notes that the dam lies at the edge of Vijayapura and Bagalkot districts. This record focuses on its documented river and irrigation role and does not repeat the portal's questionable annual-electricity unit.
source_org: Vijayapura District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page contains an annual electricity-output figure with a questionable unit; that figure is deliberately excluded. The dam is described as bordering Vijayapura and Bagalkot districts.
keywords: Vijayapura Almatti Dam Krishna River Upper Krishna Irrigation Project reservoir Bagalkot North Karnataka

title: Rainfed agriculture and soil-water measures described for Kalaburagi
content: Kalaburagi's Agriculture Department page describes the district as predominantly agrarian and outlines soil sampling and soil-health-card work, certified or truthful-labelled seed distribution, subsidized sprinkler and drip irrigation, organic farming, mechanization and watershed development. The page specifically refers to a target to issue soil health cards by the end of 2018-19, so the record is a description of the portal's programme snapshot, not confirmation that each scheme is currently available.
source_org: Kalaburagi District Administration, Government of Karnataka
reporting_year: Soil-health-card target stated through 2018-19; other page details are undated
uncertainty: The page is undated and includes a past 2018-19 target. Treat the listed programmes as a historical portal snapshot, not current scheme guidance.

title: Badami Caves and the early Chalukya capital
content: The Bagalkot district portal describes Badami, formerly Vatapi, as an early Chalukya capital and identifies its cave temples as 6th- and 7th-century monuments. The portal attributes the foundation of the town to Pulakeshi I, later building work to Kirtivarman I, and completion of the cave temples to Mangalesha. It also locates Badami near the Malaprabha River and the heritage sites of Pattadakal and Aihole.
source_org: Bagalkot District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district portal page is undated and does not provide references for its historical chronology; dates and attributions are presented as that page's account.
keywords: Badami Vatapi Bagalkot Chalukya caves Pulakeshi Kirtivarman Mangalesha Malaprabha Pattadakal Aihole history Uttara Karnataka

title: Dharwad crops beyond the cotton hybrid
content: Dharwad's district profile lists chickpea (channa), soybean and groundnut seed varieties alongside paddy and jowar, and names Alphonso mangoes and Navalur guavas among locally notable crops. This widens the profile beyond the Dharwad Cotton Hybrid already indexed, without claiming current acreage or production.
source_org: Dharwad District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district profile is undated and gives no acreage, yield, production or cultivar-release year for these crops.
keywords: Dharwad chickpea channa soybean groundnut paddy jowar Alphonso mango Navalur guava crops agriculture Uttara Karnataka

title: Hubli's commercial role and Dharwad's academic-cultural role
content: Dharwad's district profile characterizes Hubli as a commercial and industrial hub and Dharwad as an academic and cultural hub, describing them as complementary twin cities. This is a district-level urban identity distinction rather than a population or economic statistic.
source_org: Dharwad District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal does not date or quantify this characterization; it is retained as the district administration's description.
keywords: Hubli Dharwad commercial industrial academic cultural twin cities geography Uttara Karnataka

title: Kumaravyasa and Veera Narayana in Gadag's literary heritage
content: Gadag's district profile associates Kannada poet Narayanappa, popularly known as Kumaravyasa, with nearby Koliwada and the composition of Karnata Bharata Kathamanjari. It says he composed the work before Veera Narayana, his chosen deity, and identifies the Veera Narayana and Trikuteshwara temples as places of religious and historical importance. The account is attributed to the district portal.
source_org: Gadag District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district profile is undated and provides no independent scholarly citation for the biographical or authorship account.
keywords: Gadag Kumaravyasa Narayanappa Karnata Bharata Kathamanjari Koliwada Veera Narayana Trikuteshwara Kannada literature

title: Asar Mahal and Adil Shahi public architecture
content: The Vijayapura district portal dates Asar Mahal to about 1646 and attributes its construction to Mohammed Adil Shah, describing its use as a Hall of Justice. The page notes frescoes on the upper floor, a courtyard tank and the site's present maintenance by the Archaeological Survey of India. Its account also mentions a religious relic kept in the building; that tradition is not presented here as independently verified history.
source_org: Vijayapura District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal is undated and does not cite an architectural or archival source for the construction date or use; details are attributed to the district page.
keywords: Vijayapura Asar Mahal Mohammed Adil Shah 1646 Hall of Justice frescoes Adil Shahi architecture

title: Haveri's river-basin prehistory and local ruling houses
content: Haveri's district history describes prehistoric evidence in the Tungabhadra and Varada river basins and names regional ruling houses including the Kadambas of Hanagal and Nurumbad and rulers based at Bankapura and Guttal. It identifies temples at Bankapura, Rattihalli, Haveri and other localities as material traces of this history. The page's undated count of inscriptions is deliberately excluded.
source_org: Haveri District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal page is undated and gives no archaeological references; it also reports an undated inscription count that is not repeated here.
keywords: Haveri Tungabhadra Varada prehistoric Hanagal Nurumbad Bankapura Guttal Kadamba temples history Uttara Karnataka

title: Haveri's saints, writers and freedom fighters
content: Haveri's district history identifies Kanakadasa, Shishunala Sharif, Sarvajna, V. K. Gokak and other cultural figures with the district. It also names Mailara Mahadevappa and Gudleppa Hallikeri in its account of the freedom movement, associating Mahadevappa with Motebennur and Hallikeri with Hosaritti. The biographical associations are presented as the district portal's account.
source_org: Haveri District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and gives no citations or life dates for the named figures; it is a district-level biographical summary.
keywords: Haveri Kanakadasa Shishunala Sharif Sarvajna V K Gokak Mailara Mahadevappa Gudleppa Hallikeri freedom fighters saints writers

title: Shanthi Sagara lake in Channagiri taluk
content: Davanagere's district tourism page identifies Shanthi Sagara as a lake in Channagiri taluk and locates it along the Channagiri-Davanagere route. The portal also repeats an unreferenced claim that it is among Asia's largest constructed lakes; that comparative claim is not included here.
source_org: Davanagere District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and contains an unreferenced superlative, which is deliberately excluded; no lake area or hydrological measurements are asserted.
keywords: Davanagere Shanthi Sagara lake Channagiri water landscape North Karnataka

title: Chitradurga's Stone Age habitation and Paleyagara history
content: Chitradurga's district profile describes human habitation dating to the Stone Age and names successive dynasties that ruled the area. It emphasizes the Paleyagaras, saying they strengthened forts and that Chitradurga became their capital, and identifies Onake Obavva in its account of resistance to Hyder Ali. The record excludes the page's myths and presents the historical narrative as the district portal's account.
source_org: Chitradurga District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The page is undated and does not cite archaeological or historical sources; mythic material from the page is not treated as fact.
keywords: Chitradurga Stone Age Paleyagaras fort capital Onake Obavva Hyder Ali history prehistory

title: Guru Nanak Jhira and Bidar's local pilgrimage tradition
content: Bidar's places-of-interest page describes Guru Nanak Jhira as a Sikh pilgrimage site and explicitly frames the account of Guru Nanak's visit and a spring emerging from laterite rock as legend. The spring and the site's continuing religious significance are included as local tradition, not as independently established historical events or medical claims.
source_org: Bidar District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal explicitly labels the Guru Nanak visit as legend; no miracle, healing effect or historical date is asserted as fact.
keywords: Bidar Guru Nanak Jhira Sikh pilgrimage laterite spring local legend religious heritage

title: Black soils and the Krishna-Bhima plains in Yadgir
content: Yadgir's district tourism page links the region's black-cotton soils and the plains of the Krishna and Bhima rivers with settlement and landscape. This is a qualitative agro-geographic description; it does not supply a soil survey, crop-area data or production figures.
source_org: Yadgir District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The undated tourism page is not a soil survey or agricultural report; no crop or soil statistics are inferred from its description.

title: Prehistoric remains and rock markings in Yadgir
content: Yadgir's district tourism page lists prehistoric remains at Hunasagi, Budihal and Rajankollur and describes Stone Age rock markings and paintings at Balichkra. The page supplies no archaeological dating or excavation references, so this record identifies the portal's reported sites without assigning a chronology.
source_org: Yadgir District Administration, Government of Karnataka

title: Koppal dryland farming and irrigated horticultural crops
content: Koppal's district history page describes rocky terrain and monsoon-dependent dryland farming, naming jowar and groundnuts. It also says some farmers have adopted irrigation associated with Tungabhadra waters and lists pomegranates, grapes and figs among crops grown in the district. The page's export and state-ranking claims are omitted.
source_org: Koppal District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district page is undated, mixes history with agriculture, and gives no production, acreage or reporting period; its unsupported export and seed-production superlatives are not repeated.

title: Protected temples at Krauncha Giri near Sandur
content: Ballari's district tourism page identifies two protected Hindu temples in one compound at Krauncha Giri near Sandur: Kumaraswamy Temple and Parvati Temple. The page gives approximate period attributions of the 8th-10th and 7th-8th centuries respectively and presents the association of Kumaraswamy Temple with Murugan as a religious belief.
source_org: Ballari District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The portal does not cite an archaeological authority for the temple dates; the Murugan association is presented as belief, not as established history.
keywords: Ballari Krauncha Giri Sandur Kumaraswamy Parvati protected temples Murugan temple architecture

title: Ankasamudra Bird Conservation Reserve
content: Vijayanagara's district portal describes Ankasamudra as a lake associated with the Vijayanagara period and says the government declared the site a bird conservation reserve in 2017. The page notes that Tungabhadra water-filling work had begun, but gives no date for that status update; the record therefore does not present it as a current project status. Undated bird counts and lake-area figures are excluded.
source_org: Vijayanagara District Administration, Government of Karnataka
reporting_year: Bird conservation reserve designation reported as 2017
uncertainty: The portal page is undated and includes bird counts and lake area without reporting years; those figures are intentionally omitted.
keywords: Vijayanagara Ankasamudra bird conservation reserve 2017 lake Tungabhadra wetland Hagaribommanahalli

title: Jolada rotti, bele hoorana holige and tahari in Kalaburagi
content: Kalaburagi's district profile names jolada rotti served with curry and spiced peanut chutney powder, bele hoorana holige as a festival sweet, and tahari as a rice-and-meat dish. It also identifies Kannada and Urdu as prominent languages in the district. These dishes are documented as the district portal's food profile, not as an exhaustive or dated survey of household diets.
source_org: Kalaburagi District Administration, Government of Karnataka
uncertainty: The district profile is undated and does not cite an ethnographic or dietary survey; this is a descriptive portal account.
